objective: Make Treasurer the single economic admission boundary for model/API inference and API-backed ComputeOffer provisioning while preserving routing, capability, execution, and verification separation of powers.

rulesConsidered: Overseer is the sovereign command authority.
Treasurer owns economic admission and settlement.
Routers select by capability, quality, latency and physical suitability but do not authorize spend.
Workers execute but do not own economic authority.
F07 remains an independent verification boundary.

changes: Added TreasuryEconomicAdmission for model invocation pricing, hard-budget assessment, reservations and ComputeOffer admission.
Extended TreasuryPriceRegistry with model token pricing and ComputeOffer cost estimation.
Generalized Treasury execution scopes for inference and ComputeOffer resources.
Bound AIRuntime and IntelligentRouter to Treasury and propagated Overseer, mission and task identity.
Moved Treasury economic admission into the model routing loop before provider execution.
Disabled provider-internal retries when Treasury manages the economic attempt.
Exposed exact per-call provider usage for Treasury settlement when available.
Added Treasury-backed ProviderApiRegistry.provisionWithTreasury.
Added strict normal-failure release and ambiguous-provision preservation semantics.
Added Treasury-backed CapabilityFirstRouter asynchronous admission while blocking legacy synchronous production routing.
Separated inference-token capacity from compute/scarcity capacity in Treasury accounts and reservations.
Added independent token-capacity settlement/release accounting and token-capacity configuration.
Made Treasury price selection deterministic by preferring the newest active pricing version.
Documented the multidimensional Treasury resource ledger and single economic-authority rule.
Added a stateless Mongo-backed Treasury runtime accessor for callbacks and route handlers.
Moved generation entitlement admission behind TreasuryQuotaAdmission with Firestore kept as a compatibility projection.
Made /api/generate-video obtain a real Overseer economic command before model/content work.
Gated standalone script, enhancement, scene regeneration and quiz draft model endpoints through Treasury.
Converted providerFactory into a production hard Treasury gateway and retained direct fallback only for non-production compatibility.
Propagated Treasury model context through content validation, refinement, visual intelligence and WorkflowRuntime.
Demoted CostGovernor, MissionBudgetManager and AgentEconomicsEngine from production economic authorities.
Separated inference-token capacity from compute/scarcity capacity.
Added terminal-reservation idempotency protection and conservative unmeasured model-failure reconciliation.
invariants: Unknown paid model pricing is denied rather than guessed.
$0 monetary cost does not imply unlimited scarce capacity.
Each additional model/provider attempt requires a fresh Treasury reservation.
Ambiguous provider provisioning keeps its hold until reconciliation.
Treasury does not select the physical worker.
Legacy economic components are compatibility/advisory layers only during staged migration.
Inference token reservations do not consume the compute/scarcity capacity ledger.
New model attempts cannot reuse a settled or released idempotency key; each attempt has its own economic identity.
Only trusted bootstrap/configuration code seeds paid model pricing into Treasury; execution routers cannot mutate prices.

verificationResults.apiProviderFabric: SUPERSEDED/CANCELLED ON OLDER HEAD; LIVE RUN REQUIRED

notes: Treasury remains the deterministic economic authority; routers do not grant spend.
Paid model pricing is read from the Treasury price registry and unknown paid pricing is denied.
ComputeOffer provisioning is economically reserved before provider mutation.
Provider-internal retries are disabled under Treasury-managed execution.
Ambiguous provisioning retains the economic reservation until reconciliation.
Production AI/F06 execution is fail-closed when required Treasury context is absent.

conflicts.originalConflict: Model/API routers could independently decide whether a paid invocation was economically acceptable.
conflicts.proposedResolution: Keep model capability/quality/latency selection in the router but move paid economic admission, pricing and reservation into Treasury.
conflicts.acceptedResolution: IntelligentRouter and the Treasury-backed CapabilityFirstRouter path require Treasury economic admission before managed provider execution.

conflicts.originalConflict: ComputeOffer provisioning could mutate a provider resource before economic authorization.
conflicts.proposedResolution: Reserve the exact normalized offer economically before invoking provider provisioning.
conflicts.acceptedResolution: ProviderApiRegistry.provisionWithTreasury performs Treasury admission/reservation before provider mutation and releases on normal failure.

conflicts.originalConflict: Router-provided model prices could be treated as authoritative and permit stale or manipulated economics.
conflicts.proposedResolution: Only Treasury's price registry is authoritative for paid model pricing; trusted application configuration seeds it during controller boot.
conflicts.acceptedResolution: Paid model admission denies when Treasury has no active price, and router-supplied price metadata cannot mutate Treasury pricing during execution.

conflicts.originalConflict: Provider-internal retries could spend beyond the approved Treasury attempt envelope.
conflicts.proposedResolution: Disable provider-internal retries under Treasury-managed execution and require a fresh reservation for another attempt.
conflicts.acceptedResolution: BaseProviderPlugin performs one managed provider attempt; additional attempts are controlled by the outer Treasury-aware routing loop.

forgerPlan: Forge Architect, Forge Builder, Forge Security and Forge Release reviewed the migration contract and its staged compatibility boundary.
